cell.label: Pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis persisting for at least 6 months and severe enough to cause functional disability
• Consider urinalysis and culture as well as screening for chlamydia and gonorrhea. • Treat infection.

• Work up any specific abnormalities on physical examination and treat any infections. • Address any psychosocial factors and discuss possibility of symptom improvement without diagnosis, as well as possible need for multidisciplinary approach.

• Screen for alarm symptoms such as hematochezia, melena, significant weight loss, or pain severe enough to awaken from sleep. • Consider fecal occult blood testing. • Trial of diet and bowel program.
• Reevaluate. • Consider stool studies, endoscopy, referral.
Symptoms are suggestive of a gynecologic cause?
• Diagnosis unclear: early multidisciplinary approach is appropriate.
• Check urinalysis, consider culture. • Urinalysis negative symptoms suggest interstitial cystitis, conservative treatment or referral. • Hematuria without obvious infection, consider referral.
• Consider transvaginal ultrasound. • Consider trial of hormonal treatment, including combined oral contraceptive pills or a GnRH agonist for 3-6 months.
• Continue hormonal treatment. • Consider addition of NSAIDs.
